newsitem.title: USA: Knight-Ridder profits up on ad revenues, cheaper newsprint.
newsitem.headline: Knight-Ridder profits up on ad revenues, cheaper newsprint.

text.p: Knight-Ridder Inc. said Tuesday that it posted unexpectedly strong profits in the first quarter, primarily from the sale of its cable television investments, although earnings were also helped by increased advertising revenues and lower newsprint prices.

The company said it earned $174.7 million, or $1.85 a share, in the quarter, including a one-time after-tax gain of $128 million on the sale of Knight-Ridder's interest in all but one of the jointly owned cable investments it had made with Tele-Communications Inc.

Excluding the gain, the company's net income almost doubled to $46.4 million from $23.5 million. Earnings per share rose to 49 cents from 24 cents, exceeding analysts' consensus estimates of 47 cents.
The company said total operating revenues fell to $679.3 million from $697.7 million following the sale of Knight-Ridder Financial, its financial wire service subsidiary, in July 1996.
Excluding the former unit, revenues grew 4.2 percent.
"Revenue growth was very strong, and newsprint pricing -- as anticipated -- worked very much in our favour," said Ross Jones, Knight-Ridder's chief financial officer.

The Miami-based publisher of 31 daily newspapers also said it expected full-year earnings, excluding one-time gains, to rise 20 percent, as it the spends less on newsprint and advertising revenues continue to rise.
"For April, advertising revenue is well ahead of last year, with all three categories showing gains," Jones said.
"While we expect some increase in the cost of newsprint going forward, we still anticipate that for the year as a whole we will spend approximately 15 percent less on it than we did in 1996."
Knight-Ridder's stock added 37.5 cents to $36.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
